consequence.statement: XRDs using the v2 API without an explicit scope default to Namespaced XRs, which keep Crossplane fields under spec.crossplane and do not support claims; v1 XRDs default to LegacyCluster and keep claims.
consequence.remediation: Set scope explicitly (Cluster or LegacyCluster) if cluster-scoped or claim-based XRs are needed.

original.statement: The v2 CompositeResourceDefinition API adds a spec.scope field that defaults to Namespaced, so XRs are namespaced by default (v1 XRDs default to LegacyCluster).

decision.reason: [ev-4b260bcbe57b] says `scope` defaults to `Namespaced` in the new v2 XRD API. Namespaced XRs put Crossplane fields under `spec.crossplane` and don't support claims. Clusters that use the v1 XRD API still default to `LegacyCluster` and stay backward compatible. Nothing is said to fail, be rejected or stop being honoured, so the kind is behavior-change (review), and medium severity fits. One small overreach: the remediation suggests setting `LegacyCluster` explicitly on a v2 XRD, but the evidence only ties `LegacyCluster` to the v1 XRD API.
